The Incident of a Slave Woman and the Justice of Hadhrat Umar (RA)

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports that a slave woman once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) and said, "My master has accused me of fornication and made me sit on a fire until my private organ was burnt." Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked her, "Did anyone witness you commit the act?" When she replied in the negative, he asked further, "Did you make any confession before him?" When she again said that she did not, Hadhrat Umar (RA) exclaimed, "I shall deal with him." When Hadhrat Umar (RA) saw the man, he asked, "Do you punish with punishment that is reserved for Allaah (with fire)?!" The man entreated, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! I was suspicious of her." "Did you see her commit the act?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) demanded to know. "No," came the reply. Hadhrat Umar (RA) enquired further, "Did she then confess to you that she committed the act?" Again he said, "No."
Hadhrat Umar (RA) then exclaimed, "I swear by the Being Who controls my life that I would have definitely taken retribution from you had I not heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'Retribution cannot be taken from a master for anything he does to his slave and also not from a father for anything he does to his child.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) had the man lashed a hundred times and then said to the woman, "You may go because you are now freed for the pleasure of Allaah. You are now the freed slave of Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ. I testify that I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say, 'The person who is burnt by fire or disfigured by it is a free person and is the freed slave of Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ.'"[^2]
The Incident Between a Farmer and Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) and the Justice of Hadhrat Umar (RA) in the Matter

Hadhrat Makhool narrates that Hadhrat Ubaadah bin Saamit (RA) once called a non-Arab Christian farm labourer to hold his animal next to Baytul Maqdas. When the labourer refused, Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) hit him so hard that his head was cut. The labourer sought help from Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), who then asked Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA), "What made you do that to him?" Hadhrat Ubaadah (RA) replied, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen!
